mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3pp+ increase in unemployment rate over three months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of triggered periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (supply) and rise in housing starts (demand) indicates economic imbalance where supply constraints outpace demand, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of interaction events, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS rising) indicates robust economic activity and corporate hiring, boosting earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >60% of PAYEMS growth periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation above 5.0% (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) signals central bank tightening and erodes real purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of CPIAUCSL > 5.0% periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Divergence between rising retail sales (RSAFS) and falling housing starts (HOUST) signals consumer spending shift away from durable goods, indicating economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of interaction events, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production contraction (INDPRO falling >1.0% in 3 months) during supply shock regimes indicates manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of INDPRO contraction periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
